chunks: And from him, from a man, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام used to dislike salat (prayer) in the fur of every thing whose meat is not eaten.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the reported source of the ruling
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), the ritual act of worship under discussion
key_terms.لَا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: whose meat is not eaten; referring to animals not lawful for consumption
key_terms.وَبَرِ: fur or hair covering used in garments
key_terms.يَكْرَهُ: he disliked; indicates disapproval in this legal context

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat in the fur of animals whose meat is not eaten?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling related to the validity or disapproval of salat (prayer) when performed in clothing made from the fur of animals whose meat is not permissible to eat. It reflects jurisprudential guidance on proper dress in worship according to the teaching of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
